plan: My value is $40. In a second-price auction with 3 bidders, a common strategy is to bid your true value. This is a dominant strategy, meaning it's optimal regardless of what others bid. Since the other bidders are rational, they are likely to follow a similar strategy. Bidding my true value of $40 maximizes my profit by ensuring I win when I should and don't overpay.

My value is $13. In a second-price auction, bidding my true value is a dominant strategy, meaning it's the best strategy regardless of what others bid. This maximizes my profit by ensuring I win when my value is above the second-highest bid and don't pay more than my value. I will bid my value of $13.

This is a first-price sealed-bid auction with a second-price payment rule (Vickrey auction). In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value. This is because bidding below your value risks losing a profitable opportunity, and bidding above your value risks winning at a price higher than your value. Since this is the first round and I have no history to learn from, I will bid my true value.
